question: Is stance loss rare because business email is different, or because it is rare in memory writes generally? The tool only matters if the first.
reading: The failure this tool targets is domain-dependent: 55% of bad writes in conversational hearsay versus 7% in business email.
caveats: The conversational sources were CONSTRUCTED to contain hearsay, so 55% is an upper bound for that setting and not an estimate of natural conversation.

The two corpora differ in more than domain: the email set was sampled and labelled blind, the conversational set was labelled exhaustively in an earlier session. The direction is solid; the magnitude is not a clean effect size.
Even in a corpus built to contain laundering, 9 of 20 bad writes were out of scope. Extractors fail in ways beyond stance loss even where stance loss is the designed hazard.
